step1_analysis.description: A passive tuning network comprising NMOS switches and a MOS varactor. It is designed to switch capacitive loads or resistive paths into an RF circuit (like an LC tank or amplifier degeneration) to select between 2.4 GHz and 5.2 GHz bands and provide fine frequency/gain tuning for a dual-band transceiver.

paper_reference.title: A Dual-Band 5.15–5.35-GHz, 2.4–2.5-GHz 0.18-m CMOS Transceiver for 802.11a/b/g Wireless LAN

operating_frequency.description: Resonant frequency of the LC tank with the switched varactor network connected.

sky130_expected.calculation: With an external 1nH inductor and 1pF capacitor, f = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C)). C_total = 1pF + C_varactor (~20fF). f_res ≈ 5.0 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The varactor adds a small capacitance to the fixed 1pF tank, slightly lowering the 5.03 GHz ideal resonance.

tuning_range.description: Frequency shift achieved by sweeping the varactor tuning voltage.

sky130_expected.calculation: Delta C for a 5um/0.5um MOScap is ~10fF. Delta f = f_res * (Delta C / 2C) = 5e9 * (10e-15 / 2e-12) = 25 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on the small size of the varactor (W=5u, L=0.5u), the tuning range will be a fraction of the center frequency.

gain.description: Voltage gain / peaking of the tank at resonance (related to Q-factor).

sky130_expected.calculation: Tank Q is limited by the 10k parallel resistor and switch Ron (~270 ohms). Peak voltage = I * R_eff. With 1A AC, V_peak in dB will be high, reflecting the tank impedance.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The 30 dB paper metric applies to the full RX path. For this passive tank, we measure the impedance peak in dB.

output_power.description: Maximum voltage swing across the tank nodes.

sky130_expected.calculation: Transient simulation with a small current stimulus will produce a voltage swing dependent on the tank impedance.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Paper metric is for the PA. Here we just measure the transient swing of the passive network.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure the resonant frequency, tuning behavior, and transient swing of the switched varactor network by embedding it in an ideal LC tank.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Switched Varactor Network
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 N3 LABEL_NET_0 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N6 N2 N6 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N5 N4 N6 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 LABEL_NET_3 N0 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N1 N4 LABEL_NET_3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}

* Biasing and Control
V_LABEL_NET_3 LABEL_NET_3 0 0
V_N0 N0 0 1.8
V_N4 N4 0 1.8
V_LABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 1.8
V_N2 N2 0 0.9

* Tank components to simulate resonance
L5 N5 0 1n
C5 N5 0 1p
R5 N5 0 10k
I_AC5 0 N5 AC 1

L3 N3 0 1n
C3 N3 0 1p
R3 N3 0 10k
I_AC3 0 N3 AC 1

.control
* AC Analysis to find resonant frequencies
ac dec 100 1G 10G

let v5_db = vdb(N5)
let v3_db = vdb(N3)

meas ac max_v5_db max v5_db
meas ac f_res5 when v5_db=max_v5_db

meas ac max_v3_db max v3_db
meas ac f_res3 when v3_db=max_v3_db

* Transient Analysis
tran 10p 5n
meas tran v_max_n5 max v(N5)
meas tran v_min_n5 min v(N5)

print f_res5 f_res3
quit
.endc
.end
